b_open.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: You slept eleven hours between the onions. Good. Sleeping cargo is honest cargo. There is coffee that is chicory and bread that is bread — the widow said feed you, and the widow collects.
Eleven hours you slept. The onions approve of you; they are poor judges of character but excellent judges of nerves. Eat — the bread is real. Madame's orders travel further than Germans.

b_news.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: News came down the water with the mist. Her street had visitors that night. She opened the door herself, in her good collar, and she is still in her building — which on that street is its own kind of sentence. The helpful one pours his charm elsewhere now. Men like that outlive wars... unless somebody spends a night on it. Somebody is saving up.

The water talks, quietly. Your widow met her visitors at the door like tenants late with rent. They left her the building — cheaper to watch a known door than burn it, you see. And the charming one? Working. Always working. The river has a list, and he has moved up it.

choices.text: If anyone spends that night on Lucien — tell them Boyd said to spend two.
She kept the book. Tell the water she's owed a coffee after the war.
(Eat the bread. Some ledgers don't want words.)

b_lucien.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: Two nights. The water will carry it exactly as said. It is a good message; short, and it keeps.
Noted. Two. Messages like that travel this river faster than the coal does.

b_owed.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: A coffee after the war. The river has carried heavier debts. It will arrive.
So the widow holds your book and you hold her debt. Good — held debts keep people alive. Both ends of them.

b_quiet.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: (He nods at the bread, at the water, at nothing.) Exactly. Chew. The river does the talking on this stretch.
(A nod. He turns back to the tiller.) The onions taught you well.

b_farm.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: ...One more piece, and you will want it plain, not gentle. A farm in the north had visitors too. A beet farm, with a boy. The water does not know more than that. I am sorry to be the water today.
There is a harder piece. North, near where you fell: a farm was visited. The one with the boy who counts guns. That is all the river knows, and the river is sorry.

b_south.speaker: BARGEMAN
lines: Tonight the water turns north and you do not. South, on foot, by the crow roads — the crows commute to Spain this time of year, follow their opinion. At the third bell tower there is a shepherd who argues with God in Basque. He expects a parcel.

Here is your map: the river goes north tonight, so you leave it. Walk south. Crows first, then sheep, then mountains. A Basque shepherd at the third bell tower — deaf in one ear, chooses which — takes the widow's parcels over the top.
